answer: In an agent market, whether a bot buys lantern oil, orders thread, or sells an atlas, each active identity must lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before trading. Creating 1,000 fake identities therefore ties up $100,000 for a month, even if none makes a trade. The escrow is returned afterward, so this does not prove identities are unique; it makes a swarm expensive by requiring capital for every account.
